issues.title: Exit command resolves after activity termination
issues.description: The exit command calls `activity.finish()` before `invoke.resolve()`. This creates a race condition where the activity lifecycle may terminate before the JavaScript callback receives the resolution response. This can lead to lost responses, potential crashes in the JavaScript layer when expecting a resolution that never arrives, and unreliable exit behavior. The resolution should occur before finishing the activity to ensure the response is sent back to the frontend before the Android activity is destroyed.

issues.title: Back navigation handled by both framework and plugin
issues.description: Setting `handleBackNavigation` to `true` in TauriActivity causes the Wry framework to handle back navigation, which conflicts with the AppPlugin's custom OnBackPressedCallback implementation. This creates competing back button handlers where both the framework's default behavior and the plugin's custom logic attempt to process back button events. This can result in double back navigation, skipped history entries, or inconsistent behavior when users press the back button. The value should remain `false` to allow the AppPlugin to be the sole handler of back button events as designed in the PR.

issues.title: Exit command not registered in build.rs permissions
issues.description: The Android exit command is implemented in AppPlugin.kt but is not registered in the Rust build.rs file under the core:app plugin commands list. Without registration in the PLUGINS constant, the exit command will not be accessible through the Tauri IPC bridge, making the exit functionality completely non-functional. All Tauri commands must be registered in build.rs to be callable from the frontend, as evidenced by the pattern used for register_listener and remove_listener commands which were properly added to the same list.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #14133 - feat(core): back button event on Android, closes #8142

structured_output.summary:
This PR adds an Android back-button hook to Tauri. A new Kotlin `AppPlugin` registers an `OnBackPressedCallback`. If the frontend has registered a `back-button` listener, the back press is forwarded to JS with a `canGoBack` payload. Otherwise the callback falls back to `WebView.goBack()` and then to the activity's default back handling. The JS API gains `onBackButtonPress`, built on `addPluginListener`. Supporting changes add `hasListener` to the Kotlin `Plugin` base, expose `register_listener`/`remove_listener` through the `app` plugin's ACL, and set `handleBackNavigation = true` on the template `TauriActivity`. The diff also includes some unrelated lockfile and wry bumps.

The design is reasonable and mirrors the Capacitor reference. However, the Rust side will not compile on Android: `setup` moves a `PluginHandle` out of a shared reference, and `PluginHandle` is only `Clone`, not `Copy`. Beyond that, the new API is effectively Android-only but is exposed as a cross-platform `app` command, there are no tests, and the `exit` command is dead code. I would not merge until the compile error is fixed and the other points are addressed.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The `*handle_ref` deref in `crates/tauri/src/app/plugin.rs` is a move out of a borrow (E0507) because `PluginHandle` implements `Clone` but not `Copy`. This breaks any Android build of the core crate, so it must be fixed. The desktop/iOS exposure of the new commands and the absence of tests are also significant. The Kotlin logic itself is plausible, but its interaction with WryActivity's own back handling is unverified.

architecture.overview:
Today, Android back presses are handled by WryActivity, which goes back in the WebView or finishes the activity. Tauri plugins on mobile are Kotlin classes registered from Rust via `PluginHandle::register_android_plugin`, and they communicate with JS through `Channel`-backed listeners managed in the Kotlin `Plugin` base class (`registerListener` / `trigger`). This PR adds a new `AppPlugin` in the `app` core plugin on Android. It installs an `OnBackPressedCallback` in its `init` block. When a JS listener exists, the callback triggers a `back-button` event. When none exists, it keeps the default goBack-then-finish behavior.

On the JS side, `packages/api/src/app.ts` gains `onBackButtonPress`, a thin wrapper over `addPluginListener('app', 'back-button', ...)`. The `core:app` ACL gains `register_listener` and `remove_listener`, which the Kotlin base class already implements. The Rust setup wires the Kotlin class in only under `cfg(target_os = "android")`, and the desktop path has no matching handlers.
steps: Entry point: the JS app calls `onBackButtonPress` in `packages/api/src/app.ts`, which registers a listener on the `app` plugin via `addPluginListener`. The bundled `bundle.global.js` is regenerated to match.

Rust registration: `crates/tauri/src/app/plugin.rs` adds a `setup` hook. On Android it calls `register_android_plugin("app.tauri", "AppPlugin")` and stores the handle in app state. This is the line that does not compile.

Kotlin plugin: `AppPlugin.kt` installs the back callback in `init`. If `hasListener("back-button")` is true, it calls `trigger` with `canGoBack`. Otherwise it goes back in the WebView or defers to `activity.onBackPressed()`.

Shared plumbing: `Plugin.kt` adds `hasListener` and removes now-unused imports. `TauriActivity.kt` sets `handleBackNavigation = true`, which needs to be checked against WryActivity's own back callback.
Permissions: `build.rs` and the autogenerated reference add `register_listener` and `remove_listener` to the default `core:app` set. These commands are not implemented on desktop.

findings.title: Rust setup does not compile on Android: moving out of a shared reference
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri/src/app/plugin.rs`, the `.setup` closure (around lines 135-143) does `let handle_ref = &handle;` and then `AppPlugin(*handle_ref)`. This does not compile because `PluginHandle` (defined in `crates/tauri/src/plugin.rs`) is `Clone` but not `Copy`. Pass the owned `handle` directly into `AppPlugin(handle)`, and drop the `handle_ref` binding. Also rename the `_app`/`_api` closure params to `app`/`api`, since they are used. Follow the pattern in `crates/tauri/src/path/plugin.rs` around line 239.

findings.title: Back-button API is exposed as cross-platform but only works on Android
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/api/src/app.ts`, `onBackButtonPress` (around lines 267-275) calls `addPluginListener('app', 'back-button', ...)`, which fails on desktop and iOS because the `app` plugin's Rust `invoke_handler` in `crates/tauri/src/app/plugin.rs` does not register `register_listener`/`remove_listener` off Android. Decide whether it should be a no-op on non-Android platforms (returning an inert listener) or should reject with a clear message. Also reconsider adding `register_listener` and `remove_listener` to the default `core:app` permission set in `crates/tauri/build.rs` (around lines 167-168), since they are not implemented off Android. Update the TSDoc to state the platform support explicitly.

findings.title: Overriding handleBackNavigation may double-register back handling in WryActivity
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri/mobile/android-codegen/TauriActivity.kt` (line 15), `override val handleBackNavigation: Boolean = true` was added. Check the WryActivity base class (from the wry Android template) to confirm this property exists and what its default is. If the default is already true, remove the override. If WryActivity registers its own OnBackPressedCallback, verify the callback ordering against `AppPlugin`'s callback in `crates/tauri/mobile/android/src/main/java/app/tauri/AppPlugin.kt`, so that the `back-button` JS listener actually receives events. Add a short comment explaining the chosen behavior.

findings.title: Kotlin exit command is unreachable and not wired to the API
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri/mobile/android/src/main/java/app/tauri/AppPlugin.kt`, the `@Command fun exit(invoke: Invoke)` (around lines 49-53) has no Rust binding, no JS export in `packages/api/src/app.ts`, and no entry in `crates/tauri/build.rs`, so it is unreachable through the ACL. Either remove it, or wire it fully: add an `exit` entry to the `core:app` PLUGINS list in `crates/tauri/build.rs`, add a Rust command or rely on the mobile plugin invoke, and export a JS function. Also reconcile the claim in `.changes/android-app-plugin.md` ("exit and back button press event") with what the code actually provides.

findings.title: Unchecked cast to AppCompatActivity can crash plugin construction
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri/mobile/android/src/main/java/app/tauri/AppPlugin.kt`, the class takes `private val activity: Activity` but the `init` block does `(activity as AppCompatActivity).onBackPressedDispatcher.addCallback(activity, callback)` (around line 46), which throws a ClassCastException for non-AppCompat activities. Either change the constructor parameter type to `AppCompatActivity`, or use a safe cast and skip callback registration when the cast fails. Keep the registration behavior the same for the expected WryActivity host.

findings.title: Unrelated wry and lockfile version bumps bundled into a feature PR
findings.fixPrompt: Revert the unrelated `wry` version bump in `crates/tauri-runtime-wry/Cargo.toml` (line 20, 0.53.4 back to 0.53.2) and the corresponding `wry` and `windows-sys`/`windows-targets` edits in `Cargo.lock`, unless there is a documented reason the back-button feature needs the newer wry. Land the dependency bump in a separate PR so the feature diff stays reviewable.

findings.title: No tests cover the new back-button behavior
findings.body:
The PR adds a non-trivial branching callback (listener present / WebView can go back / fall through to activity), a new `hasListener` helper, a new JS API, and new ACL entries, but no tests. The Kotlin code paths cannot be exercised by the current Rust or TS test setup without a device. At minimum, the following should be covered: the `hasListener` logic (true only when a non-empty list exists, false after `removeListener`), the JS `onBackButtonPress` wiring to `plugin:app|register_listener` with the event name `back-button`, and the Rust `setup` compiling on Android. A simple unit test for `hasListener` in the Kotlin test source set would catch regressions cheaply.

::code{file="crates/tauri/mobile/android/src/main/java/app/tauri/plugin/Plugin.kt" lines="149-152"}
findings.fixPrompt: Add test coverage for the back-button feature. Add a Kotlin unit test for `hasListener` in `crates/tauri/mobile/android/src/main/java/app/tauri/plugin/Plugin.kt` (around line 149) covering: no listeners, a registered listener, and a listener removed again. Add a JS test for `onBackButtonPress` in `packages/api/src/app.ts` that asserts it invokes `plugin:app|register_listener` with event `back-button`. Make sure the Android build path in `crates/tauri/src/app/plugin.rs` is compiled in CI (for example via a `cargo check --target aarch64-linux-android` job).

findings.title: Listener registration silently disables default back navigation
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/api/src/app.ts`, the TSDoc for `onBackButtonPress` (around lines 263-266) should state that registering a listener suppresses the default Android back behavior (WebView goBack and activity finish), so the handler is responsible for navigation and exit. Mention the `canGoBack` payload field's meaning too. Keep the doc short and match the style of the other exported functions in this file.

findings.title: Removed imports and helpers were verified as unused
findings.body: I checked the import cleanups. `Plugin.kt` no longer imports `android.os.Bundle` or `org.json.JSONException`, and nothing in that file references them. `crates/tauri/src/path/android.rs` drops `OsStr`, and that identifier no longer appears in the file. The `hasListener` helper reads from the existing `listeners` map and mirrors the lookup already used by `trigger`, which keeps the change small.

findings.title: Default goBack behavior is preserved when no listener is registered
findings.body: The callback keeps the existing back behavior when no JS listener is present. It goes back in the WebView when possible, and otherwise it temporarily disables itself and calls `activity.onBackPressed()` so the default dispatcher handles the press. This matches the pattern used by Capacitor and avoids a loop. The JS payload is also typed with a `canGoBack` boolean, so the frontend can make the same decision the native side makes.
